sections.title: Reporting with that-clauses
sections.content:
When we report what someone said or thought, we often use a that-clause after a reporting verb:
• He said (that) he was enjoying his new job.
Also: accept, admit, agree, announce, claim, complain, confess, explain, mention, promise, reply, suggest.
Some of these verbs must have an object + that-clause in the active:
• She reminded me that I had to be there by 10. (not She reminded that ...)
Also: advise, assure, inform, notify, persuade, promise, reassure, tell, warn.

sections.title: Verbs with "to" + object + that-clause
sections.content:
With other verbs we can include an object, but we must use the preposition to before it:
• I mentioned to them that there was a problem. (not I mentioned them that ...)
Also: admit, announce, complain, confess, explain, mention, point out, propose, prove, reply, say, suggest, whisper.

sections.title: Reporting with other patterns
sections.content:
We can also report what someone says using other patterns:
• verb + to-infinitive: He offered to help. / She promised to come.
• verb + object + to-infinitive: They told us to wait. / I asked him to go.
• verb + -ing: He suggested going to the cinema. / She denied stealing the money.

exercises.question: The police ___ that they had captured the suspect.
exercises.hint: Announce doesn't need an object before the that-clause; told does.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: announced
Announce doesn't need an object before the that-clause; told does.

exercises.sentence: She said me that she would be late for the meeting.
exercises.correction: She told me that she would be late for the meeting.
acceptable: She told me that she would be late
exercises.hint: 'Say' does not take a personal object — 'tell' does. 'Said me' is always wrong.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: She told me that she would be late
'Say' and 'tell' are the two main reporting verbs but they have different structures: SAY: say (that)... / say something — no personal object before 'that'. TELL: tell someone (that)... — must have a personal object. 'Said me that' is always wrong; use 'told me that'.

exercises.question: She ___ me that she would be late.
exercises.hint: Inform needs an object; said doesn't take an object directly before the that-clause.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: informed
Inform needs an object; said doesn't take an object directly before the that-clause.

exercises.sentence: He told that the meeting had been cancelled.
exercises.correction: He said that the meeting had been cancelled.
acceptable: He said that the meeting had been cancelled.
He told us that the meeting had been cancelled.
exercises.hint: 'Tell' must have a personal object: 'told us/me/them/her/him'. Without an object, use 'say'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: He said that / He told us that
'Tell' always requires a personal object before 'that': 'told me', 'told us', 'told them'. Without a personal object, use 'said'. You cannot say 'He told that...' — it must be 'He told someone that...'

exercises.question: I ___ that I had made a mistake.
exercises.hint: Confess requires 'to' before the person being confessed to.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: confessed to them
Confess requires 'to' before the person being confessed to. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.sentence: They informed that the flight would be delayed by two hours.
exercises.correction: They informed us that the flight would be delayed by two hours.
exercises.hint: 'Inform' requires a personal object before 'that' — like 'tell'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: They informed us that
Like 'tell', 'inform' and 'notify' require a personal object before 'that': 'informed us/me/passengers/the authorities'. 'Informed that' with no object is incorrect. Contrast with 'announced that', 'confirmed that', 'stated that' — these do not require an object.

exercises.question: He ___ that we should meet earlier.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: suggested to us
Suggest takes 'to' + object + that-clause.

exercises.prompt: Report what someone said using correct tense backshift:
exercises.hint: told + person + that + subject + past perfect passive
exercises.explanation:
Answer: She told him that the meeting had been cancelled
Reported speech structure: reporting verb (told) + personal object (him) + that + reported clause. In the reported clause, 'has been cancelled' (present perfect passive) shifts back to 'had been cancelled' (past perfect passive). 'Told' always requires a personal object.

exercises.question: They ___ us to leave the building immediately.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: ordered
Order + object + to-infinitive. This verb pattern requires a to-infinitive as its complement.

exercises.question: We ___ for another hour.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: agreed to wait
Agree + to-infinitive. This verb pattern requires a to-infinitive as its complement.
